newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian M2 money supply up 5.5 percent in July.
newsitem.headline: Romanian M2 money supply up 5.5 percent in July.

text.p: Romania's M2 money supply rose 5.5 percent in July, below monthly inflation of 7.5 percent, National Bank (BNR) data showed.
ROMANIAN MONEY SUPPLY JULY JUNE JULY 1995
NOTES -- Broad money grew by a year-on-year 69.1 percent in July, when it stepped up 23.5 percent from last December.
The BNR said M1 narrow money, which includes currency outside banks and demand deposits, rose 6.7 percent to 7.8 trillion lei at end-July with cash in circulation almost flat at 3.94 trillion lei.
Demand deposits soared 14.2 percent to 3.9 trillion lei at end-July, fuelling inflation fears, a BNR report said.
It said July household savings of 7.1 trillion lei slid in real terms, pressured by troubles in two Romanian private banks. It said the drop was also triggered by the summer holiday.
Residents' hard currency deposits was 22.8 percent of total broad money in July, up from June's 22.2 percent. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
